answer:
Yes. Kilimanjaro is one of the world's most popular high-altitude treks, and people with no technical mountaineering experience climb it all the time. Most routes are walk-ups that don't need ropes or climbing gear. The trip usually takes 5 to 9 days on one of several official routes, such as Machame, Marangu, Lemosho, Rongai or the Northern Circuit [1][2].

You can't go on your own, though. Since 1991, Tanzanian law has required every climber to go with a licensed guide registered with Kilimanjaro National Park, and you need a park permit, which a tour operator normally arranges [3]. The hardest part is the altitude, not the terrain. Around 70–80% of climbers reach the summit on average, and longer itineraries that give your body more time to adjust have much higher success rates than rushed 5-day climbs [4].
